>_ Episode 2 · Jul 16, 2026 · 1h 10m

The ASI Delusion: Why You Can’t Out-Code Reality

Play Episode 2 on YouTube
Watch on YouTube SpotifyApple Podcasts

"We're not going to be able to kill it. We're not going to be able to stop it..."

Welcome back to Philosophy Programs and Prompts. In this episode, Casey (@OntologyExplained) and Carl (@InternetOfBugs ) take a hard, realistic look at Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI). While tech founders and doomer non-profits stand to gain massive clicks and capital by pitching a looming, god-like AI deity, the actual engineering constraints paint a completely different story.

We deconstruct the core arguments driving the ASI panic: from the flawed chess masters analogy to the physical impossibility of infinite recursive self-improvement. More importantly, we discuss how abstract "human extinction" narratives are actively distracting us from real, pressing AI harms happening right now—including deepfakes, non-consensual intimate imagery, and mental health crises. Grounded in real-world software engineering and academic philosophy, we explore why an AI god won't fix global resource allocation, and why power disparities will likely remain human-led endeavors.
